title: Regional soft-credit reservoir to stabilize limiter outages and preserve SLOs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Intermittent limiter control-plane outages and partial state loss in region handoffs have resulted in transient but material SLO violations (elevated 5xx, tail latency spikes due to retries, and unfair token exhaustion for long-running tenants). Existing fallback behavior currently drops requests aggressively or routes to lower-tier variants without preserving tenant fairness or SLO targets.

Proposal: Introduce a regional "soft-credit reservoir" layer that temporarily backs limiter admission when primary limiter state is degraded or disconnected. The reservoir is a bounded, ephemeral credit pool per-region (with optional per-tenant soft allocations) that can be consumed deterministically during control-plane interruptions and during multi-region failover windows. The reservoir preserves weighted fairness guarantees, limits worst-case debt accumulation, and triggers reconciliation flows once the limiter state is healthy.

Key design goals: preserve p99 latency SLOs for high-tier customers during short limiter outages, avoid catastrophic global drops, maintain proportional fairness by tenant weight, provide deterministic bounded cost exposure, and enable predictable reconciliation without double-counting tokens.

High-level components: (1) Reservoir admission layer: small, fast in-path actor with local soft-credits; (2) Lease/lease-refresh protocol: short leases (e.g., 5–30s) to bound reservoir exposure; (3) Regional exchange protocol: limited, periodic scoreboard sync to reconcile consumed credits across replicas after recovery; (4) Debt reconciliation worker: background process to reconcile usage vs. actual quota and emit compensating telemetry/alerts.

Why different from existing approaches: instead of a single global emergency bucket or hard drops, the soft-credit reservoir preserves proportional fairness and gives applications a deterministic buffer during windowed outages while keeping fail-open exposure bounded by explicit credits and TTLs.

Non-goals: This is not a replacement for long-term quota expansion or primary limiter redesign. It does not attempt to provide durable cross-region consensus; reconciliation is eventual and conservative.
acceptance_criteria: During synthetic control-plane outage tests, reservoir prevents SLO breaches in canary region: p99 latency stays within target and 5xx spike reduced by >= 80% compared to 'drop-only' baseline
Fairness preserved: top-10 tenants' relative share deviation (post-reconciliation) < 10% under mixed workloads in outage window
Bounded exposure: aggregate reservoir consumption across region <= configured regional-reservoir-capacity in all chaos tests
Reconciliation correctness: total billed tokens post-reconcile equals actual request tokens minus reservoir offsets with audit logs and no double-billing
Operational runbook and metrics present: dashboards for reservoir usage, outstanding debt, reconciliation duration, and emergency rollbacks
tasks: Design proto: define reservoir token model, lease TTL, refill policy, and fairness algorithm (weighted leaky-bucket) (Asha)
Implement admission layer in limiter hot path (C++) with 3 code paths: normal, reservoir-consume, reject (Miguel)
Lease and scoreboard proto: compact protobuf + HTTP/Grpc shim; implement optimistic scoreboard sync (Eng infra)
Debt reconciliation worker: idempotent reconcile loop with audit record emission (SRE)
Integration tests: chaos mesh scenarios to simulate limiter control-plane loss, multi-region failover, and network partitions
Create console dashboard and SLO alerts; add feature flag and canary rollout controls
Perf benchmarks on p99 and CPU overhead; iterate on kernel fast path to keep added latency < 200us
notes: Soft-credit reservoir per-region defaults: 200k tokens total, soft-alloc per-tenant based on recent 24h consumption percentile
Leases expire quickly to limit exposure; default TTL 15s with jitter to avoid stampedes
Reconciliation will prefer negative adjustments to consumption (compensations) and will never auto-increase tenant quota; any permanent credit grants handled via billing pipeline
Telemetry: expose reservoir.consume_rate, reservoir.available, reservoir.debt_outstanding, reconcile.duration, reconcile.errors
Cost considerations: small bounded additional compute in hot path; tradeoff is SLO preservation vs. small potential billing complexity during reconciliation

Security: reservoir admissions only allowed while limiter reports degraded or disconnected; normal path unchanged. Security review scoped to audit logging of reconciliation - set to false for initial spike but will be re-evaluated
